facts.says: Iron armour is plain dark-grey metal.
Iron is the second-weakest armour metal, a step above bronze, and anyone can wear it without any training.
A middling smith can hammer iron armour out of iron bars on an anvil; an iron platebody takes a good few bars.
Iron platebodies are sold over the counter at Horvik's armour shop in Varrock.
Steel armour is a light, silvery grey, paler and brighter than iron.
Steel is made by smelting iron ore together with coal, and the bars are then smithed into armour on an anvil.
Steel armour is stronger than iron but still near the bottom of the metals, and it needs only a little combat training to wear.
Steel platebodies can be bought ready-made at Horvik's armour shop in Varrock.
Dragon armour is a hard, dark-red metal, and the platebody has a black design across the chest and little spikes at the shoulders.
The dragon full helm is spiked and so dear that people wear it more to show off their wealth than for the fighting.

Most dragon armour can't be smithed from ore; the pieces are rare finds off fierce monsters such as metal dragons, and fetch a high price. Only a master smith at the Dragon Forge can make the platebody.
Nobody can wear dragon armour without a good deal of defensive training, and the platebody is only for those who have slain a dragon.
Dragon full helms come only from the mithril dragons of the Ancient Cavern, either straight off a dragon or from a barbarian spirit called up with their chewed bones.
An abyssal whip is a long, segmented lash of dark red and black that ends in a barbed point.
The whip is a weapon from the Abyss, dropped by abyssal demons, and only a well-trained fighter can wield one.
An abyssal whip is made from the spine of an abyssal demon.
The whip is one of the most common weapons among serious fighters: quick, strong and not too dear.
A rune scimitar is a wicked curved sword with a blade of teal-coloured runite.
Only a near-master smith can forge a rune scimitar from runite bars, though fire giants and Zamorak warriors sometimes drop them.
The rune scimitar is the second-best scimitar there is, beaten only by the dragon one.
A dragon scimitar has a jagged, blood-red curved blade on a dark grey hilt.
The dragon scimitar is the strongest scimitar there is, and it can't be smithed from raw metal.
Dragon scimitars are sold by Daga, a monkey smith on Ape Atoll, and only those who have finished the monkeys' troubles there may wield one.
When one fighter strikes another with a dragon scimitar's special attack, it can knock out the victim's protective prayers for a short while.
Green d'hide armour is made from scaly green dragon leather, and the shield is a maple shield covered in the same green hide.
Green d'hide is real dragonhide, worn by archers rather than swordsmen.
The hides come from green dragons, which live out in the Wilderness, where hunters of them often get set upon by other fighters.
Only someone who has proven themselves a dragon slayer may wear a green d'hide body.
The graceful outfit is pale, near-white hooded clothing with black trim and touches of teal and red, and the hood covers most of the face.
Graceful clothing is very light, and wearing it helps a runner get their breath back faster, more so with the full set on.
Graceful can't be bought with coins; it's paid for with marks of grace, little tokens that turn up on rooftop and agility courses for those who run laps.
Grace sells the graceful outfit in the Rogues' Den, under the Toad and Chicken inn in Burthorpe.
Osten in Shayzien will dye graceful clothing in the colours of the Kourend houses, for a price in marks of grace.
Barrows gear comes in six sets, each named for the brother who wore it: Ahrim, Dharok, Guthan, Karil, Torag and Verac.
Dharok's armour is dark, greenish-grey plate studded with yellowed spikes, and it goes with a huge greataxe.
Barrows gear is won from the crypts of six undead brothers buried under mounds in southern Morytania; they were once famous Saradominist warriors from a small town in Misthalin.
Barrows gear wears down with fighting and stops working until it's mended; Bob the axe seller in Lumbridge and Dunstan the Burthorpe smith both repair it.
A full set of Dharok's hits harder the more badly hurt its wearer is.
A fire cape looks like molten rock, mottled orange and gold, and its pattern shifts and flows as if it were burning.
A fire cape is earned by surviving every wave of the TzHaar Fight Cave and then beating TzTok-Jad at the end.
A fire cape can't be bought or traded; lose one and the only way to get another is to beat the Fight Cave again.
For all its flames, a fire cape gives off no light at all.
The TzHaar guards will only let you into the inner city of Mor Ul Rek if you show them a fire cape.
An infernal cape looks like a sheet of cooled black rock, cracked in a honeycomb with glowing orange lava between the plates, and it moves as if alive.
An infernal cape is won by beating TzKal-Zuk at the bottom of the Inferno, and it is the strongest cape a fighter can wear, better even than the fire cape.
An infernal cape is, in effect, a cape made of lava, which seems an odd thing to want to wear.
To get into the Inferno at all, you have to hand over a fire cape to the TzHaar as the price of entry.
A partyhat is a crown-shaped hat with jagged points, all in one bright colour: red, yellow, blue, purple, green or white, and there are black, rainbow and silver ones too.
Partyhats come out of Christmas crackers, which have to be pulled with somebody else, and they only turn up around Christmas.
Whoever pulls a Christmas cracker gets to pick the partyhat colour, and both people get one.
Patchy in Mos Le'Harmless will stitch a blue partyhat and a pair of sagacious spectacles together into one partyhat and specs.
A max cape is a long red cape edged in gold, with red gems set in gold on its back and a pale collar at the neck.
The max cape is only for those who have reached the highest level in every single skill, and nobody else can even put one on.
Max capes are sold by Mac, who lives on a little island west of the Warriors' Guild that only the most skilled can reach, and he charges a fortune.
When someone buys their first max cape, Hans and the Wise Old Man send them their congratulations by magic.
A twisted bow has gnarled black limbs streaked with white, hooked tips, and a yellow-green string.
The twisted bow is carved from the twisted remains of the Great Olm, the creature in the deepest part of the Chambers of Xeric.
Twisted bows are a rare reward from the Chambers of Xeric, the caves under Mount Quidamortem in Kebos, and they are among the most valuable weapons there are.
The more magic a foe has in it, the harder a twisted bow hits it.
The Void Knight top is black and dark grey, crossed by a white band, with a white zig-zag emblem on the chest.
Void gear is the armour of the order of the Void Knights, and it's never sold for coins.
The Void Knights hand out their armour only to those who earn their commendation by helping fight off the pests that pour out of portals at their island outpost.
Void gear needs a fair bit of training in every kind of fighting, and a full set works with whichever helm is worn: melee, ranged or magic.
A squire on the Port Sarim docks ferries fighters out to the Void Knights' Outpost.
The plain Saradomin cape is deep blue with a pale yellow hem, hung from a silvery clasp.
A Saradomin cape is a gift from the god Saradomin himself to a battle mage who has proven themselves.
The cape is won at the Mage Arena deep in the Wilderness: you beat Kolodion in all four of his forms, step through the sparkling pool, and pray at Saradomin's statue.
A battle mage wearing the Saradomin cape and carrying Saradomin's staff can charge up the Saradomin Strike spell to hit much harder.
An imbued Saradomin cape has been charged with great power using trophies from the Mage Arena's second trial, and it is among the best capes a mage can wear.
A skillcape shows that its wearer has reached the highest level there is in one skill.
Each skillcape is a long cape in its skill's own colours with the skill's emblem on the back, and it comes with a matching hood; the cooking cape is purple.
Skillcapes are bought for a hefty sum from each skill's master, who wears one proudly and keeps to a place that suits the skill.
Someone who has mastered more than one skill wears their capes with a trim of a different colour along the edge.
Each skillcape has its own small blessing: nobody wearing a cooking cape ever burns their food, and a firemaking cape works as a light that never goes out.
Rocky is a small dark-grey raccoon; Red is a red panda and Ziggy a tanuki, the same pet in other shapes.
Rocky very rarely takes up with someone who steals a great deal, from picking pockets to raiding market stalls, and follows them about from then on.
Feed Rocky redberries and he becomes Red the red panda, poison ivy berries make him Ziggy the tanuki, and white berries turn him back.
The beaver is a small, dark-brown beaver that looks like it has chewed through a great deal of wood.
A beaver very rarely turns up to follow someone who chops a great many trees.
With a funky shaped log from the Forestry Shop, a beaver can be changed to the colour of whatever logs it's given, and it can even be turned into a pheasant or a fox.
The heron is a grey wading bird on long legs, fond of fishing; the great blue heron is a blue version of the same pet.
A heron very rarely comes to follow someone who fishes a great deal.
Feeding a heron a great heap of spirit flakes turns it into a great blue heron, and any raw fish turns it back.
A rock golem is a little walking figure of brown stone.
A rock golem very rarely breaks loose to follow someone who mines a great deal.
Give a rock golem a lump of ore and it takes on that ore's colour; a plain rock turns it back.
